answer: At block timestamp T, an agent stakes compute to join the network. Trust transfers at that exact sealed moment—not before, not after. Like timber felled along a river, the stake drifts to a single verification vertex where validators burn it. Burned stake cannot re-enter the river because the block hash at T already consumed that commitment. Replay the same timestamp and validators see a spent hash. Sybils must cut fresh timber every attempt, and timber costs more than forged identities ever repay.
